pr.title: Show an unnamed agent session by the last group of its ID
pr.head: 36736883000f99eae19e525d448af2242a7b306a

summary: Projector lets agent sessions find and message one another. An unnamed session needs a display label so you can tell which session sent or received a message.

Codex uses time-ordered session IDs. Their first eight characters can match for sessions started close together. This change displays the final 12-character group instead, through one shared helper. Named sessions keep their names, and commands still address unnamed sessions by their full IDs.

cards.title: Review validation
cards.html:
• The configured gate and exact-head CI passed.
  • The new label regressions exercise list output, message output, stable labels, and non-UUID IDs.
  • The broader focused run exposes an existing keychain test error on Python 3.15.2 and 3.12.16. The same error reproduces at the merge base.

groups.title: Use one stable label for unnamed sessions
groups.kicker: Display a random session-ID suffix wherever an agent is named
intro: A session ID is the full value that identifies an agent conversation. The display label is shorter and does not control message routing. short_id takes the last UUID group, or the last 12 characters of another ID, without consulting other sessions.

The shared label logic now reaches list and registration output, message previews, read headers, send confirmations, and errors. Messages keep their full sender IDs, so stored messages need no migration.

files.note: Centralizes suffix labels and applies them to sender displays.

checks.text: Traced every label caller and the recipient lookup: names still win, and routing and JSON records continue to use full session IDs.

groups.title: Keep display labels distinct and consistent
groups.kicker: Exercise the labels through the CLI and retain relay lifecycle coverage
intro: The new tests create two Codex sessions with the same time prefix. They check that the CLI displays different labels and that a message preview agrees with the later list and read output.
The relay tests continue to check generated summaries reaching another machine. Their row filters now use the label helper so those tests stay focused on summary delivery.

files.note: Adds CLI regressions for shared prefixes, stable message labels, and arbitrary session IDs.
Updates two relay row filters to recognize the new display labels.

checks.text: The unchanged keychain fallback test starts one mock patch twice. It raises “Patch is already started” on Python 3.15.2 and 3.12.16; the merge-base reproduction confirms this predates the label change.

groups.title: Explain which ID to display and which to send to
groups.kicker: Document the suffix label and keep full IDs as command inputs
intro: The CLI reference explains why time-based prefixes collide and gives two distinguishable examples. The agent messaging skill describes unnamed sessions by the same suffix, while its send instructions continue to require a name or full session ID.

files.note: Describes suffix labels, non-UUID fallback, and unchanged send addressing.
Updates peer discovery to describe the session-ID suffix.
